ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a five-membered cyclic imide anion, the nitrogen atom on the ring is marked with a negative charge, and there are two carbonyl groups in the ring. On the right side is a positively charged sulfur center; the sulfur is connected to two methyl groups and connected to a chlorine atom. A curved arrow points from the imide nitrogen to sulfur, and another curved arrow indicates that the S–Cl bond electrons move toward chlorine. Reasoning: According to the arrow pushing, the electron pair of nitrogen forms a new N–S bond with sulfur; the S–Cl bond breaks, and chlorine becomes a separate chloride ion. The imide ring and the two carbonyl groups remain unchanged, and sulfur is still positively charged and retains two methyl groups. According to the answer format of the question, the unchanged spectator fragment *C(*)O is also included. Therefore the SMILES of the product state is *C(*)O.C[S+](C)N1C(=O)CCC1=O.[Cl-].
